sanskrit: sarvam etad atikramya vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ yan naḥ kṣamaṃ mahābāho tad bravīhy avicārayan
english: Setting all of this aside, and having pondered again and again, O mighty-armed one, tell us without hesitation what is fitting for us.

sanskrit: śrutvaitad dharmarājasya dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ meghadundubhinirghoṣaḥ kṛṣṇo vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard these words of the Dharma King, which were filled with righteousness and purpose, Kṛṣṇa, whose voice resounds like the thunder of clouds and drums, spoke.

sanskrit: uktavān asmi yad vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam na tu tan nikṛtiprajñe kauravye pratitiṣṭhati
english: I have spoken words that were beneficial, full of righteousness and purpose — but they do not take hold in that Kaurava whose mind is bent on wickedness.

sanskrit: na ca bhīṣmasya durmedhāḥ śṛṇoti vidurasya vā mama vā bhāṣitaṃ kiṃ cit sarvam evātivartate
english: That fool of wicked intellect heeds not the counsel of Bhīṣma, nor of Vidura, nor of me — he transgresses all of it entirely.

sanskrit: na sa kāmayate dharmaṃ na sa kāmayate yaśaḥ jitaṃ sa manyate sarvaṃ durātmā karṇam āśritaḥ
english: He desires neither righteousness nor glory; that wicked soul, relying on Karṇa, believes he has already conquered all.

sanskrit: bandham ājñāpayām āsa mama cāpi suyodhanaḥ na ca taṃ labdhavān kāmaṃ durātmā śāsanātigaḥ
english: Suyodhana even ordered my arrest, yet that wicked transgressor of all order did not obtain his desire.

sanskrit: na ca bhīṣmo na ca droṇo yuktaṃ tatrāhatur vacaḥ sarve tam anuvartante ṛte viduram acyuta
english: Neither Bhīṣma nor Droṇa uttered a fitting word on that occasion; all follow him except Vidura, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: śakuniḥ saubalaś caiva karṇaduḥśāsanāv api tvayy ayuktāny abhāṣanta mūḍhā mūḍham amarṣaṇam
english: Śakuni, the son of Subala, and also Karṇa and Duḥśāsana — those fools spoke unseemly words against you, O impatient one, to a fool.

sanskrit: kiṃ ca tena mayoktena yāny abhāṣanta kauravāḥ saṃkṣepeṇa durātmāsau na yuktaṃ tvayi vartate
english: And what use was what I said? Whatever the Kauravas spoke, in brief — that wicked soul does not conduct himself fittingly toward you.

sanskrit: na pārthiveṣu sarveṣu ya ime tava sainikāḥ yat pāpaṃ yan na kalyāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tasmin pratiṣṭhitam
english: Among all the kings and among all these soldiers of yours, whatever is sinful and whatever is not wholesome — all of that is established in him.

sanskrit: na cāpi vayam atyarthaṃ parityāgena karhi cit kauravaiḥ śamam icchāmas tatra yuddham anantaram
english: Nor do we at all desire peace with the Kauravas through excessive concession — after that, war is the only recourse.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā pārthivāḥ sarve vāsudevasya bhāṣitam abruvanto mukhaṃ rājñaḥ samudaikṣanta bhārata
english: Having heard these words of Vāsudeva, all the kings, O Bhārata, looked silently at the face of the king, saying nothing.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tv abhiprāyam upalabhya mahīkṣitām yogam ājñāpayām āsa bhīmārjunayamaiḥ saha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, perceiving the intent of the kings, ordered the march together with Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins.

sanskrit: tataḥ kilakilābhūtam anīkaṃ pāṇḍavasya ha ājñāpite tadā yoge samahṛṣyanta sainikāḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava's army broke into a great tumult of joyful cries, and when the march was ordered, the soldiers rejoiced exceedingly.

sanskrit: avadhyānāṃ vadhaṃ paśyan dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ niṣṭanan bhīmasenaṃ ca vijayaṃ cedam abravīt
english: The Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira, seeing the slaughter of those who should not be slain, groaned and spoke thus to Bhīmasena and Vijaya:

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ vanavāsaś ca prāptaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca yan mayā so 'yam asmān upaity eva paro 'narthaḥ prayatnataḥ
english: That great calamity for whose sake the forest exile was endured, and the suffering I have borne — that very calamity now comes upon us despite all our efforts.

sanskrit: yasmin yatnaḥ kṛto 'smābhiḥ sa no hīnaḥ prayatnataḥ akṛte tu prayatne 'smān upāvṛttaḥ kalir mahān
english: The goal for which we have exerted ourselves has failed us in our endeavour; yet without our effort, this great calamity would have returned to us all the same.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hy avadhyaiḥ saṃgrāmaḥ kāryaḥ saha bhaviṣyati kathaṃ hatvā gurūn vṛddhān vijayo no bhaviṣyati
english: How indeed shall we wage battle with those who should not be slain? How shall victory be ours after killing our elders and venerable ones?

sanskrit: tac chrutvā dharmarājasya savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ yad uktaṃ vāsudevena śrāvayām āsa tad vacaḥ
english: Hearing this from the Dharma King, Savyasācī, the scorcher of foes, caused him to hear again what Vāsudeva had said.

sanskrit: uktavān devakīputraḥ kuntyāś ca vidurasya ca vacanaṃ tat tvayā rājan nikhilenāvadhāritam
english: The son of Devakī has spoken, and O king, you have heard in full the counsels of Kuntī and of Vidura.

sanskrit: na ca tau vakṣyato 'dharmam iti me naiṣṭhikī matiḥ na cāpi yuktaṃ kaunteya nivartitum ayudhyataḥ
english: My firm conviction is that neither of those two would counsel unrighteousness; nor, O son of Kuntī, is it proper to turn back without fighting.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vāsudevo 'pi savyasācivacas tadā smayamāno 'bravīt pārtham evam etad iti bruvan
english: Hearing those words of Savyasācī, Vāsudeva too smiled and spoke to Pārtha, saying: "It is even so."

sanskrit: tatas te dhṛtasaṃkalpā yuddhāya sahasainikāḥ pāṇḍaveyā mahārāja tāṃ rātriṃ sukham āvasan
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, O great king, resolved upon war, dwelt that night in comfort together with their soldiers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vyuṣitāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu rājā duryodhanas tataḥ vyabhajat tāny anīkāni daśa caikaṃ ca bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the night had passed, King Duryodhana then arrayed those armies — eleven in all, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: narahastirathāśvānāṃ sāraṃ madhyaṃ ca phalgu ca sarveṣv eteṣu anīkeṣu saṃdideśa mahīpatiḥ
english: Among foot-soldiers, elephants, chariots, and horses — the excellent, the middling, and the inferior — the king of the earth assigned each to all these divisions.

sanskrit: sānukarṣāḥ satūṇīrāḥ savarūthāḥ satomarāḥ sopāsaṅgāḥ saśaktīkāḥ saniṣaṅgāḥ sapothikāḥ
english: Equipped with drag-ropes and quivers, with chariot bodies and lances, with sword-sheaths and javelins, with arrow-pouches and bludgeons —

sanskrit: sadhvajāḥ sapatākāś ca saśarāsanatomarāḥ rajjubhiś ca vicitrābhiḥ sapāśāḥ saparistarāḥ
english: With standards and banners, with bows and javelins, with variegated ropes, with nooses and protective armour —

sanskrit: sakacagrahavikṣepāḥ satailaguḍavālukāḥ sāśīviṣaghaṭāḥ sarve sasarjarasapāṃsavaḥ
english: With hair-grasping flings, with oil, molasses, and sand, all furnished with pots of venomous serpents, and with resin-sap and dust —

sanskrit: saghaṇṭāphalakāḥ sarve vāsīvṛkṣādanānvitāḥ vyāghracarmaparīvārā vṛtāś ca dvīpicarmabhiḥ
english: All equipped with bells and shields, with axes and wood-cutters, covered with tiger skins and clad in leopard hides —

sanskrit: savastayaḥ saśṛṅgāś ca saprāsavividhāyudhāḥ sakuṭhārāḥ sakuddālāḥ satailakṣaumasarpiṣaḥ
english: With bandages and horns, with pikes and various weapons, with axes and mattocks, with oil, linen, and ghee —

sanskrit: citrānīkāḥ suvapuṣo jvalitā iva pāvakāḥ tathā kavacinaḥ śūrāḥ śastreṣu kṛtaniśramāḥ
english: The ranks were splendid, the men well-formed, blazing like fires — those armoured heroes, practiced and skilled in weapons.

sanskrit: kulīnā hayayonijñāḥ sārathye viniveśitāḥ baddhāriṣṭā baddhakakṣyā baddhadhvajapatākinaḥ
english: Of noble birth, versed in the breeding of horses, installed as charioteers — with protective charms bound on, with girths fastened, with standards and banners secured.

sanskrit: caturyujo rathāḥ sarve sarve śastrasamāyutāḥ saṃhṛṣṭavāhanāḥ sarve sarve śataśarāsanāḥ
english: All the chariots were drawn by four horses, all were fully armed with weapons, all had spirited mounts, and all were equipped with a hundred bows.

sanskrit: dhuryayor hayayor ekas tathānyau pārṣṇisārathī tau cāpi rathināṃ śreṣṭhau rathī ca hayavit tathā
english: One man managed the two draft horses, two others served as rear-guard charioteers, and those two were the finest among chariot warriors — and the chariot warrior himself was likewise an expert in horses.

sanskrit: nagarāṇīva guptāni durādeyāni śatrubhiḥ āsan rathasahasrāṇi hemamālīni sarvaśaḥ
english: There were thousands of chariots, garlanded with gold all around, like well-guarded cities difficult for enemies to assail.

sanskrit: yathā rathās tathā nāgā baddhakakṣyā svalaṃkṛtāḥ babhūvuḥ sapta puruṣā ratnavanta ivādrayaḥ
english: Just as the chariots, so too the elephants — with girths fastened and richly adorned — had seven men each, like gem-bearing mountains.

sanskrit: dvāv aṅkuśadharau teṣu dvāv uttamadhanurdharau dvau varāsidharau rājann ekaḥ śaktipatākadhṛk
english: Of these seven, two bore elephant-hooks, two bore the finest bows, two bore excellent swords, O king, and one bore a lance and a banner.

sanskrit: gajair mattaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ savarmāyudhakośakaiḥ tad babhūva balaṃ rājan kauravyasya sahasraśaḥ
english: That force of the Kaurava, O king, was filled with thousands of maddened elephants bearing armour, weapons, and housings.

sanskrit: vicitrakavacāmuktaiḥ sapatākaiḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ sādibhiś copasaṃpannā āsann ayutaśo hayāḥ
english: There were tens of thousands of horses, adorned with variegated armour and ornaments, bearing banners, and accompanied by cavalry.

sanskrit: susaṃgrāhāḥ susaṃtoṣā hemabhāṇḍaparicchadāḥ anekaśatasāhasrās te ca sādivaśe sthitāḥ
english: Easily handled and well-contented, with golden trappings and equipment — those many hundreds of thousands stood under the command of the cavalry.

sanskrit: nānārūpavikārāś ca nānākavacaśastriṇaḥ padātino narās tatra babhūvur hemamālinaḥ
english: There also were foot-soldiers of various forms and kinds, wearing armour of many types and bearing weapons, garlanded with gold.

sanskrit: rathasyāsan daśa gajā gajasya daśa vājinaḥ narā daśa hayasyāsan pādarakṣāḥ samantataḥ
english: To each chariot belonged ten elephants; to each elephant, ten horses; and ten men served as foot-guards around each horse on all sides.

sanskrit: rathasya nāgāḥ pañcāśan nāgasyāsañ śataṃ hayāḥ hayasya puruṣāḥ sapta bhinnasaṃdhānakāriṇaḥ
english: Fifty elephants were allotted to each chariot; a hundred horses to each elephant; and seven men to each horse, skilled in mending and binding wounds.

sanskrit: senā pañcaśataṃ nāgā rathās tāvanta eva ca daśasenā ca pṛtanā pṛtanā daśavāhinī
english: A sena consists of five hundred elephants and the same number of chariots; ten senas make a pritana, and ten pritanas make a vahini.

sanskrit: vāhinī pṛtanā senā dhvajinī sādinī camūḥ akṣauhiṇīti paryāyair niruktātha varūthinī evaṃ vyūḍhāny anīkāni kauraveyeṇa dhīmatā
english: Vahini, pritana, sena, dhvajini, sadini, camu — these are the synonymous terms for an akshauhini, also called varuthi. In this manner the armies were arrayed by the wise Kaurava.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo daśaikā ca saṃkhyātāḥ sapta caiva ha akṣauhiṇyas tu saptaiva pāṇḍavānām abhūd balam akṣauhiṇyo daśaikā ca kauravāṇām abhūd balam
english: Eleven akshauhinis in all, and also seven — the strength of the Pāṇḍavas was seven akshauhinis, while the strength of the Kauravas was eleven akshauhinis.

sanskrit: narāṇāṃ pañcapañcāśad eṣā pattir vidhīyate senāmukhaṃ ca tisras tā gulma ity abhisaṃjñitaḥ
english: A patti consists of fifty-five men; three such senamukhas make a gulma, as it is named.

sanskrit: daśa gulmā gaṇas tv āsīd gaṇās tv ayutaśo 'bhavan duryodhanasya senāsu yotsyamānāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Ten gulmas made a gana; and ganas numbering ten thousand were the fighters ready for battle in Duryodhana's armies.

sanskrit: tatra duryodhano rājā śūrān buddhimato narān prasamīkṣya mahābāhuś cakre senāpatīṃs tadā
english: There, the mighty-armed King Duryodhana, having carefully considered brave and wise men, then appointed generals.

sanskrit: pṛthag akṣauhiṇīnāṃ ca praṇetṝn narasattamān vidhipūrvaṃ samānīya pārthivān abhyaṣecayat
english: He gathered the leading commanders of the separate akshauhinis — the finest of men — and consecrated those kings with due rite.

sanskrit: kṛpaṃ droṇaṃ ca śalyaṃ ca saindhavaṃ ca mahāratham sudakṣiṇaṃ ca kāmbojaṃ kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca
english: Kṛpa, Droṇa, Śalya, the great chariot-warrior Saindhava, Sudakṣiṇa of Kāmboja, and Kṛtavarman —

sanskrit: droṇaputraṃ ca karṇaṃ ca bhūriśravasam eva ca śakuniṃ saubalaṃ caiva bāhlīkaṃ ca mahāratham
english: The son of Droṇa, and Karṇa, and Bhūriśravas, and Śakuni the son of Subala, and the great chariot-warrior Bahlika —

sanskrit: divase divase teṣāṃ prativelaṃ ca bhārata cakre sa vividhāḥ saṃjñāḥ pratyakṣaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Day after day, and at every watch, O Bhārata, he arranged various signals among them, and confirmed them in his own presence again and again.

sanskrit: tathā viniyatāḥ sarve ye ca teṣāṃ padānugāḥ babhūvuḥ sainikā rājan rājñaḥ priyacikīrṣavaḥ
english: Thus all of them were disciplined, and those soldiers who followed in their footsteps, O king, were desirous of pleasing the king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śāṃtanavaṃ bhīṣmaṃ prāñjalir dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ saha sarvair mahīpālair idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with folded hands, along with all the kings of the earth, addressed Bhīṣma the son of Shantanu with these words:

sanskrit: ṛte senāpraṇetāraṃ pṛtanā sumahaty api dīryate yuddham āsādya pipīlikapuṭaṃ yathā
english: Without a commander of the army, even the greatest force, when it meets battle, falls apart like an anthill.

sanskrit: na hi jātu dvayor buddhiḥ samā bhavati karhi cit śauryaṃ ca nāma netṝṇāṃ spardhate ca parasparam
english: The minds of two commanders are never alike at any time, and the valour of leaders by its very nature rivals itself.

sanskrit: śrūyate ca mahāprājña haihayān amitaujasaḥ abhyayur brāhmaṇāḥ sarve samucchritakuśadhvajāḥ
english: It is heard, O greatly wise one, that against the Haihayas of immeasurable might, all the Brāhmaṇas advanced, bearing aloft banners of sacred kusha-grass.

sanskrit: tān anvayus tadā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś caiva pitāmaha ekatas tu trayo varṇā ekataḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: After them followed the Vaiśyas and also the Śūdras, O Grandsire — on one side the three varnas together, and on the other the bulls among Kṣatriyas alone.

sanskrit: te sma yuddheṣv abhajyanta trayo varṇāḥ punaḥ punaḥ kṣatriyās tu jayanty eva bahulaṃ caikato balam
english: The three varnas were routed in battle again and again, while the Kṣatriyas alone, though a numerous force on one side, kept winning.

sanskrit: tatas te kṣatriyān eva papracchur dvijasattamāḥ tebhyaḥ śaśaṃsur dharmajñā yāthātathyaṃ pitāmaha
english: Then those best of twice-born ones questioned the Kṣatriyas themselves, and those who knew dharma declared to them the truth of the matter, O Grandsire.

sanskrit: vayam ekasya śṛṇumo mahābuddhimato raṇe bhavantas tu pṛthak sarve svabuddhivaśavartinaḥ
english: We follow a single man of great intelligence in battle, but you are all separately following the dictates of your own individual minds.

sanskrit: tatas te brāhmaṇāś cakrur ekaṃ senāpatiṃ dvijam nayeṣu kuśalaṃ śūram ajayan kṣatriyāṃs tataḥ
english: Then those Brāhmaṇas appointed a single twice-born general, skilled in statecraft and brave, and thereafter they defeated the Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: evaṃ ye kuśalaṃ śūraṃ hite sthitam akalmaṣam senāpatiṃ prakurvanti te jayanti raṇe ripūn
english: Thus, those who appoint as general a man skilled, brave, devoted to the good, and free from sin — they conquer their enemies in battle.

sanskrit: bhavān uśanasā tulyo hitaiṣī ca sadā mama asaṃhāryaḥ sthito dharme sa naḥ senāpatir bhava
english: You are equal to Uśanas, and you are always a well-wisher of mine; immovable, established in dharma — be our general.

sanskrit: raśmīvatām ivādityo vīrudhām iva candramāḥ kubera iva yakṣāṇāṃ marutām iva vāsavaḥ
english: As the sun is to the rays of light, as the moon to the creeping plants, as Kubera to the yakshas, as Vāsava to the Maruts —

sanskrit: parvatānāṃ yathā meruḥ suparṇaḥ patatām iva kumāra iva bhūtānāṃ vasūnām iva havyavāṭ
english: As Mount Meru is to mountains, as Suparṇa to birds, as Kumāra to beings, as Havyavat to the Vasus —

sanskrit: bhavatā hi vayaṃ guptāḥ śakreṇeva divaukasaḥ anādhṛṣyā bhaviṣyāmas tridaśānām api dhruvam
english: Protected by you, we shall be as the dwellers of heaven protected by Śakra — truly unassailable even by the thirty gods.

sanskrit: prayātu no bhavān agre devānām iva pāvakiḥ vayaṃ tvām anuyāsyāmaḥ saurabheyā ivarṣabham
english: May you march ahead of us as Pavaki leads the gods; we shall follow you as the sons of Surabhī follow the bull.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi bhārata yathaiva hi bhavanto me tathaiva mama pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: O mighty-armed one, it is even as you say, O Bhārata; just as you are to me, so too are the Pāṇḍavas to me.

sanskrit: api caiva maya śreyo vācyaṃ teṣāṃ narādhipa yoddhavyaṃ tu tavārthāya yathā sa samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: And yet, O lord of men, I must speak what is good for them; but I shall fight for your cause, as that agreement was made.

sanskrit: na tu paśyāmi yoddhāram ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ bhuvi ṛte tasmān naravyāghrāt kuntīputrād dhanaṃjayāt
english: But I see no warrior on earth who is my equal, save only that tiger among men, the son of Kuntī, Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: sa hi veda mahābāhur divyāny astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ na tu māṃ vivṛto yuddhe jātu yudhyeta pāṇḍavaḥ
english: That mighty-armed one knows all the divine weapons in their entirety; yet the Pāṇḍava would never fight me openly in battle.

sanskrit: ahaṃ sa ca kṣaṇenaiva nirmanuṣyam idaṃ jagat kuryāṃ śastrabalenaiva sasurāsurarākṣasam
english: He and I together could in a single moment, by the sheer force of our weapons, empty this world of men — gods, asuras, and rakshasas included.

sanskrit: na tv evotsādanīyā me pāṇḍoḥ putrā narādhipa tasmād yodhān haniṣyāmi prayogeṇāyutaṃ sadā
english: But the sons of Pāṇḍu are not to be annihilated by me, O lord of men; therefore I shall always slay ten thousand warriors each day through my skill.

sanskrit: evam eṣāṃ kariṣyāmi nidhanaṃ kurunandana na cet te māṃ haniṣyanti pūrvam eva samāgame
english: Thus I shall bring about the destruction of their forces, O delight of the Kurus — unless they slay me first when battle is joined.

sanskrit: senāpatis tv ahaṃ rājan samayenāpareṇa te bhaviṣyāmi yathākāmaṃ tan me śrotum ihārhasi
english: But I shall be your general, O king, upon another condition of my own choosing — you ought to hear it from me now.

sanskrit: karṇo vā yudhyatāṃ pūrvam ahaṃ vā pṛthivīpate spardhate hi sadātyarthaṃ sūtaputro mayā raṇe
english: Either Karṇa shall fight first, or I shall, O lord of the earth — for the son of a charioteer constantly and excessively rivals me in battle.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca nāhaṃ jīvati gāṅgeye yotsye rājan kathaṃ cana hate bhīṣme tu yotsyāmi saha gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Karṇa said: I shall not fight in any manner, O king, while the son of the Gaṅgā lives; but when Bhīṣma is slain, I shall fight with the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ senāpatiṃ cakre vidhivad bhūridakṣiṇam dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajo bhīṣmaṃ so 'bhiṣikto vyarocata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with due rite and lavish gifts, installed Bhīṣma as general; and he, thus consecrated, shone resplendent.
